# Independent audit: attained affine-invariant buffered bad minima

Source: `candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb`, all
seven sections. **PASS**, with its original minimal-bad-base hypotheses
and fixed positive continuous dimension retained.

The new continuity argument was derived independently in
`candidate b096cc2ab4c584d9`.
The relevant canonical-lift parity Sections 5--6 were also reread.

The dependency order is correct. Original bad-minor minimality first
gives a uniform positive fiber-mass lower bound on the WHOLE original
sublevel beta_0<=b. The original restriction inequality and canonical
lift are applied to original depth only. The positive limiting-mass
support is closed by anchored Minkowski inclusion, and its mass tends
to one. A proper such support would violate its original minor target.
No false restriction inequality for normalized buffering enters.

Parity is preserved by the canonical lift and additive on dependence
components, so the substitution of gamma_d/k for the obsolete arbitrary
finite-base numerical target is justified by the cited arithmetic
dependency. The lifted lattice rank is not substituted for the original
occupied parity budget.

The old diameter-propagation and representation-matrix normalization
then apply to the entire sublevel. The residual centroid array is
bounded after one ACTUAL affine shear, since the representation-
preserving arrays are affine on the chosen canonical base. The
normalization maps may be selected discontinuously: the proof uses
only their existence and the compactness of the resulting representative
set. The positive mass lower bound excludes degenerate limit fibers.

The new objective is invariant under every normalization map used.
The ratio E/M cancels the continuous determinant; within-fiber
covariance transforms as A Sigma A^T and ignores fiber translations
and affine shears. The transformed continuous covector and corrected
base tilt preserve the actual buffered inequality exactly. Thus the
attained minimum is unrestricted over compatible positive shapes on
the fixed base, not merely a minimum in an artificial normal form.

The all-direction continuity proof is uniform in the unbounded base
tilt. At two candidates on the SAME base, that tilt cancels from their
threshold difference. Euclidean unit continuous normals give a uniform
slab estimate, while total variation controls body changes. Closed
pure-base caps keep the same finite subset of fibers and cost at most
the total variation error. Marked energy continuity, including boundary
marks, and covariance continuity complete the proof. Consequently the
maximum buffered depth is continuous under positive fiberwise
Hausdorff limits, jointly in epsilon.

The reference epsilon bound is strict at its stated endpoint. Late
minimizing sequences remain in the original sublevel because
beta_0<=beta_epsilon<b. Compactification preserves the objective, so
the positive limit attains its infimum. Testing an original minimizer
gives beta_0^*<=beta_epsilon^*<=beta_0^*+epsilon L R; compact normalized
limits of buffered minimizers therefore attain the original infimum.

Finally, the uniform own-properness choice is not circular. Every
buffered maximum has raw depth at least gamma_d/|P| from a largest
fiber's ordinary centroid. The uniform strip error transfers this to
a positive original depth at its source. Original within-fiber depth
is uniformly Lipschitz and zero on the own boundary, the latter by
the finite support-height LP dual. Thus the source is uniformly far
from that boundary before choosing the buffered minimizer. One fixed
smaller epsilon makes every shifted own section proper throughout the
compact class.

The theorem supplies an attained variational setting. It does not
supply the signed payment, regularity of supporting OTHER-fiber traces,
or an OC proof. Exact supporting-trace directional inverses are treated
separately rather than inferred from this compactness argument.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
